rules.description: Level 74.167 m is below the configured TEST/prototype (not official) warning level 75.0 m.
River trend FALLING at -0.245 m/h (below the prototype rise rate 0.1 m/h).
69.8 mm in the past 24 h (model analysis); prototype breakpoints {'MODERATE': 64.5, 'HIGH': 115.6} mm.
4.73 mm forecast for the next 24 h; prototype breakpoints {'MODERATE': 64.5, 'HIGH': 204.5} mm.
Heavy rainfall but the river is not (yet) rising notably. River response can lag rainfall (assumed up to 24 h), so a steady river does not lower the rainfall-based level.

trace: River evidence usable (grade SIMULATED, freshness FRESH, recent quality ACCEPTABLE).
Risk level MODERATE from the highest hazard indicator.
uncertainties: Thresholds are configured TEST/prototype (not official): TEST VALUES - not official; chosen above the 2021-2025 CWC telemetry's usual high-flow band (about 74.8-75.0 m RL) for software testing only.

The river may still respond to recent or forecast rain within ~24 h. Assumed. The real lag between basin rainfall and the river at Upper Anicut is unknown here; it depends on where the rain falls and on upstream reservoir operations (e.g. Mettur), which are not ingested.
All inputs are FABRICATED test data. This assessment describes a simulation, not the actual river.
No validated flood model exists for this site, so no flood probability is given.

scenarios.name: NORMAL
scenarios.label: Normal
scenarios.description: Stable river well below the TEST warning level, with small natural fluctuations; light rain.

scenarios.name: ALERT
scenarios.label: Alert
scenarios.description: River rising gradually towards and across the TEST warning level (not the danger level), with small fluctuations; heavy rain observed and forecast.

scenarios.name: EMERGENCY
scenarios.label: Emergency
scenarios.description: River rising substantially above the TEST danger level to a sustained peak; heavy rain with an extremely heavy forecast; riverside evacuation road closed.

scenarios.name: RECOVERY
scenarios.label: Recovery
scenarios.description: River declining gradually from an elevated level, with fluctuations; rain easing; the closed road reopens after 4 simulated hours. At an already normal level the river simply stays low.

scenarios.name: FULL_CYCLE
scenarios.label: Full flood cycle (automatic)
scenarios.description: Conditions move NORMAL -> ALERT -> EMERGENCY -> RECOVERY on a fixed simulated-hour schedule. The disaster state follows only when the evidence satisfies the state manager's rules.
